category_title: Older preschool children expressing specific anxieties about environmental and relational consistency
minimal_context: The student is participating in a journal writing activity to reflect on the upcoming move to a new school.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's work on our feeling journals today. Please draw or write about the upcoming move to the new school.

STUDENT: (Looking at the pictures of the current preschool) I feel a little nervous. This is where we did this project.

TUTOR: Just write down what you are thinking about.

STUDENT: I will miss the playground because I would play here.

TUTOR: Keep drawing in your journal.

STUDENT: (Pushes the journal away) I don’t want to move. I like this school.

options.A: Provide a less frequent schedule of breaks intermittently for the student during the journal writing activity throughout the transition.
options.B: Implement the use of autocorrect and text prediction functions on digital devices for the student to use during the journal writing activity throughout the transition.
options.C: Address the refinement of content and mechanics during the journal writing process, guiding the student from the first draft to the final copy throughout the transition.
options.D: Apply tape in 'house-like' shapes, post pictures of the preschools, and provide a makeshift moving truck with packing supplies, encouraging exploration by co-playing and asking questions.
